_doc: Leaders' letters between neighbouring districts and the news of their peace, pacts and wars (sim/civic/district-letters, sim/contrib/district-polity). Vars: fromLeader, toLeader, fromDistrict, toDistrict, other, otherLeader, speaker, leader, n, cost.

greeting.title: A letter from {fromDistrict}
body: To {toLeader}, from {fromLeader} of {fromDistrict}. The roads between us are open and our hearths are no colder than yours. Write when you can; a quiet border is worth the ink.
{fromLeader} of {fromDistrict} to {toLeader}: our harvest was thin but honest. We hope yours was kinder. Let our riders keep finding each other.
From {fromLeader}, at the seat of {fromDistrict}. We heard your people kept their fires through the cold. Tell them they are spoken of well here.

trade.title: Word on the pact, from {fromDistrict}
body: {fromLeader} to {toLeader}: the carts came through as promised. Our pact holds, and folk here have stopped asking whether it will.
To {toLeader}. The pact between {fromDistrict} and {toDistrict} keeps bread on tables that had none. {fromLeader} sends thanks, and a list of what we can spare next.

grievance.title: A sharp letter from {fromDistrict}
body: {fromLeader} of {fromDistrict} to {toLeader}: your people preach against ours at the boundary stones. We will not be told how to keep our own fires. Mend this, or we will.
To {toLeader}. Our folk are hungry and they are looking across the border while they are hungry. {fromLeader} would rather write this than send something worse.

truce.title: Terms from {fromDistrict}
body: {fromLeader} to {toLeader}: enough. Send our levies home and we will send yours. Let the road between us be a road again.
To {toLeader}, from {fromLeader}. There is no winning left in this. We lay it down, if you will.

greeting: the border is quiet and they mean to keep it so
they write as a neighbour writes
trade: the pact holds and the carts keep coming
they list what they can spare us
grievance: they will not be preached at across the border
they are hungry and they say it plainly

letter_in: {leader} has a letter from {otherLeader} of {other}, and reads it out at the seat: {gist}.
A rider from {other} came in at first light. {leader} says {otherLeader} writes that {gist}.
pact: {speaker} says {leader} and {otherLeader} of {other} have shaken on a pact. Carts will go both ways.
Word at the well: a trade pact with {other}. {speaker} says it is the first good news in weeks.
pact_broken: {speaker} says the pact with {other} is off. Nobody agrees on whose fault it was.
The carts from {other} have stopped. {speaker} says {leader} tore up the pact, or {otherLeader} did.
war: {speaker} says it is war with {other}. {leader} has called for levies.
Drums at the seat. {speaker} says {other} has crossed the boundary stones and {leader} means to answer.
levy: {n} grown folk went with the levy this morning. {speaker} watched them go.
{speaker} says {n} of ours marched for the war with {other}. The fields will miss them.
war_food: {speaker} says the war with {other} is eating the stores: the levy has to be fed.
The levy's wagons took grain again. {speaker} is counting what is left.
truce: {speaker} says there is a truce with {other}. {held}
The war with {other} is over. {speaker} says {held}
levy_home: {n} of the levy came home at dusk. {speaker} says they do not talk about it.
The levy is back: {n} walked in. {speaker} says {fallen}
far_war: {speaker} heard from a carter that {a} and {b} are at war.
{speaker} says {a} and {b} have come to blows. The trunk road between them is closed.
far_truce: {speaker} says {a} and {b} have made a truce.

won: we held the field, they say.
lost: we gave ground, and it shows.
brokered: terms were struck before either side broke.
the leaders wrote their way out of it.

none: every one of them came back.
some: not all of them came back.

ask: {leader} spreads a map on the table. "{relations}"
peace_ok: {leader} hears you out, then sends for ink. "I will write to {otherLeader} tonight. If they are as tired as we are, the war is over."
"For you, then." {leader} seals a letter of terms for {other}. By morning the levies are told to come home.
peace_no: {leader} shakes their head. "{otherLeader} would laugh at terms from us. Not yet."
"You don't know {other} as I do. They will not stop because we ask."
pact_ok: {leader} turns it over and nods. "A pact with {other}, then. I'll put my name to it if {otherLeader} puts theirs." They do.
"Carts both ways." {leader} writes to {otherLeader} while you wait. A pact with {other} is sealed.
pact_no: {leader} frowns. "{other} doesn't trust us enough for that. Letters first."
"A pact? With {otherLeader}?" {leader} laughs, not kindly. "Give it time."
poor: You haven't the spark left to move {leader} today ({cost} needed).
done: "I have written once today on your word," {leader} says. "Let it travel."
